finding: Serving captures use predetermined client durations; live-policy runner uses replay-selected durations. Full kernel-evidence online loop is not demonstrated.

finding: Saved controller_state fields mainly encode suspicious/idle; figure describes a richer lifecycle than the historical serving runner.

finding: All five L4 microbenchmark manifests specify window_seconds=5.0.
next_action: Report per-experiment settings; do not describe all windows as 10 s.

finding: L4 manifests request 2 s automatic and 8 s fixed workload segments. Reported 12–24 s values time the entire profile subprocess.
next_action: Separate requested duration, capture interval and subprocess wall time; recover capture metadata or rerun.

claim: Latency trigger is p95 / initial p95 >1.5
finding: Serving ratio is current mean / first-window mean; healthy baseline may already be anomalous.
next_action: Use independently collected healthy baseline and consistent statistics.

finding: Serving runner default is 0.10 s; complete historical serving launch arguments are not archived. A parameter table is not evidence that a value was used.

claim: Unknowns excluded from K=2 stability; cheap candidate can seed streak
finding: Original replay counted repeated unknowns; serving streaks used truth-derived labels. Cheap-to-T2 confirmation rule is not demonstrated. Step 002 repairs future mechanics.
next_action: Replace results with fresh evidence; explicitly document streak eligibility.

claim: Six-burst cap and no reported live exhaustion
finding: L4 live microbenchmark manifests cap at one burst; six is a replay cap, historically not always enforced.
next_action: Separate live/replay caps; report forced stops explicitly.

claim: Diagnoses are independently assigned from tier-visible cheap/kernel patterns
finding: Historical serving labels/score boosts read workload truth; microbenchmark branches read workload identity. Kernel summaries are stored separately, not used for the claimed serving classification.
next_action: Replace diagnosis results; independently validate references and integrate T2 classification.

claim: Model/GPU/software settings and CUDA graph behavior
finding: L4 microbenchmark manifest verifies L4/torch/CUDA/nsys; equivalent serving/A100 manifests were not found. Server logs may support subsets. Kernel visibility does not prove causal diagnosis.
next_action: Archive complete manifests for every new run; verify graph-capture coverage on GPU.

finding: Saved aggregates reproduce displayed values, but measure profile subprocess wall time under different fixed workload durations.

claim: Expected match=1.0 for every microbenchmark row
finding: Expected labels and workload-specific classifier rules are coupled.

claim: One burst in all 30 repetitions; sigma=0
finding: One burst is traceable in saved comparisons, but L4 cap=1 makes zero variation insufficient evidence of adaptive convergence.

next_action: Recompute run-level uncertainty for corrected estimands; do not call this active-capture precision.
